requirement: Read a customer CSV export where identifiers and postal codes have leading zeros and the country code NA is a real value, while blank cells still count as missing.
skeleton: REQUIRED, TEXT_COLUMNS and MISSING_MARKERS constants and load_customers reading with string dtypes, keep_default_na False and blank-only na_values, then rejecting missing required columns.
caption: Loading a customer CSV with pandas without corrupting identifier columns. load_customers(text) wraps the text in io.StringIO and calls pd.read_csv with dtype TEXT_COLUMNS mapping customer_id, zip and country to str so leading zeros survive, keep_default_na False so words like NA and NULL stay literal values, and na_values MISSING_MARKERS so only blank cells become missing. Other columns such as balance are inferred as numbers. It then checks the REQUIRED columns customer_id, zip, country and balance and raises ValueError listing the absent ones sorted and comma separated as missing columns. The fixture asserts that ids 007 and 0042 and zips 02134 and 00501 keep their zeros, that countries NA and NULL are kept as text, that only the blank zip is missing, that balance is a float column summing to 13.75, and that a CSV without zip raises ValueError matching missing columns: zip.

plan.intent: Import customer records from a CRM export
constraints: customer_id, zip and country are read as strings
NA and NULL are not treated as missing
balance is parsed as a number

rationale.teaches: Pin text dtypes and replace pandas default NA markers so the parser does not reinterpret codes and country names.
rationale.why: Default inference strips leading zeros from codes, and the default NA list turns Namibia and literal NULL strings into missing values.

ops.docstring: Load a customer CSV without mangling codes or reading NA as missing.

ops.source:
def load_customers(text: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Parse ``text`` keeping code columns as strings; only blanks are missing."""
    frame = pd.read_csv(
        io.StringIO(text),
        dtype=TEXT_COLUMNS,
        keep_default_na=False,
        na_values=MISSING_MARKERS,
    )
    missing = sorted(set(REQUIRED) - set(frame.columns))
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"missing columns: {', '.join(missing)}")
    return frame

candidates.why_wrong: Identifier columns are inferred as numbers and lose their leading zeros.
The country code NA and the text NULL are read as missing values.
Blank zip cells are kept as empty strings instead of missing.
A CSV without required columns is accepted silently.
Postal codes are inferred as floats, turning 02134 into 2134.0.
